summary.headline: Balrampur Chini's sugar segment PBIT rose 166% to INR140 crore in Q2 FY27, while the distillery stayed squeezed by unrevised ethanol prices.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a strong result in a seasonally weak, non-crushing quarter, driven by higher volumes and firmer domestic sugar realisations. The 2025-26 season ended tighter than expected, with closing stock of 3.6 million tonnes, and management expects lower output in Maharashtra and Karnataka in 2026-27 while UP stays stable. The distillery remained under pressure because ethanol procurement prices have not been revised in three years while FRP rose about 16% over the same period. An interim dividend of INR4 per share was declared, and the 80,000 TPA PLA project is on track for commissioning around end-November with INR2,400 crore spent by 15 October.

segments.name: Sugar
segments.commentary: PBIT up 166% YoY to INR140 crore on strong volume and better realisations from firm domestic prices, partly offset by cost pressure linked to the West Asia crisis.

segments.name: Distillery / Ethanol
segments.commentary: Margins compressed because ethanol procurement prices have not been revised for three years, while FRP rose about 16% over the same period. Management pointed to a UP State Advised Price announcement still pending.

segments.name: PLA (new business)
segments.commentary: 80,000 TPA plant expected to commence operations in November 2026; first institutional order from a government entity secured. Management guided against quarterly guidance for the next two quarters.

guidance_outlook: 2026-27 sugar production expected to decline, mainly in Maharashtra and Karnataka due to El Nino; UP expected relatively stable. Domestic prices expected to stay firm.

Management's own estimate: about 3 million tonnes of imports needed (range 2.5-3.5 million tonnes) to rebuild inventory from ~16 lakh tonnes; government has allowed a 10 lakh tonne TRQ as a first step.
Balrampur cane availability expected about 2% lower than last year (10.4 crore quintals crushed in 2025-26); recovery initially lower after rain damage.

Ethanol production for ESY 2026-27 expected at 18-20 crore litres, including about 8-9 crore litres from C-heavy, about 3 crore litres ENA, and the rest from maize and rice; Maizapur grain distillery intended to run at 8-9 crore litres subject to feedstock.
PLA plant to be commissioned end-November 2026; management asked investors not to guide PLA quarterly for the next two quarters and said a projection could come in about six months.
capex_capacity: 80,000 TPA PLA project on track; commissioning targeted for end-November 2026 (UP-based, per call), with INR2,400 crore spent by 15 October 2026.
Crushing: UP plants start in phases, central UP after Deepavali and east UP around 20 November 2026 (10 plants in UP).
Peak ethanol production about 28 crore litres in the prior year; current scenario allows 18-20 crore litres.
Future PLA capacity expansion: management said new capacity capex should be much lower given the initial plant's setup, and UP incentive windows will not be allowed to lapse.
demand_pricing: Management is positive on sugar prices but declined to give a number; said an average of INR60/kg is not unrealistic and a sub-INR50 average is not realistic.
Import parity and global sugar prices are rising; management expects imports to come in if global prices ease.
PLA prices rose about 10% in the last six months; PLA cost pressure from higher cane and sugar transfer prices and sulfur up 20%.
PLA demand: significant share of PLA could go to FSSAI-driven pan masala packaging demand; testing protocols passed, government mandate nearing completion.
Plastic price gap versus PLA has narrowed as food prices rose, making PLA easier to sell than a year ago, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Q1 to Q2 realisation gain (about INR4.8/kg) not reflected fully in EBIT, given no crushing in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fixed overheads such as depreciation, factory maintenance and heavy repairs in the non-operating quarter are charged to P&L with no incremental production; this reverses in Q3 and Q4 and is a yearly pattern.

qa_highlights.question: Import requirement for the season?
qa_highlights.answer: Balrampur's estimate of about 3 million tonnes (range 2.5-3.5 million) needed to rebuild inventory from about 16 lakh tonnes; no official import contract data yet and ISMA estimates not released.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of cane price (FRP/SAP) increase on EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Each INR10 per quintal increase in cane price adds about INR100 crore of raw material cost on about 10 crore quintal crush; UP government sets the cane price and announcement expected by November.

qa_highlights.question: PLA biodegradability and competitiveness versus conventional plastic?
qa_highlights.answer: Avantika Saraogi said PLA passes the most stringent international industrial compostability standard and biodegrades in the environment over time; price gap with conventional plastic has narrowed.

qa_highlights.question: Ethanol feedstock mix and maize economics for 2026-27?
qa_highlights.answer: Total ethanol 18-20 crore litres: 8-9 crore litres C-heavy, about 3 crore litres ENA, rest maize and rice (allocation pending). At current maize prices, management said grain-based ethanol is leaving margin on the table.

qa_highlights.question: Cane crushing and recovery outlook for 2026-27?
qa_highlights.answer: Cane availability could be about 2% lower than last year's 10.4 crore quintals; recovery expected lower initially after unseasonal rain, with red rot now zero; variety 20016 being multiplied, 15-20% area coverage in about two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins for PLA be guided?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give PLA margin guidance; cost will be known after production starts, and investors were asked not to expect quarterly guidance for two quarters.

risks_watch: Ethanol procurement prices unrevised for three years against FRP up about 16%; UP State Advised Price (cane price) announcement pending and could raise costs by about INR100 crore per INR10/quintal.
PLA commissioning (end-November 2026), ramp-up, yield, chemical consumption and actual conversion cost not yet disclosed; management asked for patience for about six months.
Sugar supply deficit and import policy: about 3 million tonnes import need depends on government policy and global prices.
Cane availability possibly 2% lower and early recovery risk after unseasonal rain.
Maize price increase is squeezing grain-based ethanol economics; tender outcome for grain ethanol (about 8 crore litres) pending.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the sugar business and PLA marketing progress, but deliberately cautious and non-committal on PLA margins, PLA revenue projections, cane price impact and sugar price levels. Management repeatedly deferred numbers to a later call.
key_quotes: Strong volume coupled with improved realization resulted in sugar segment PBIT to increase by 166% to INR140 crores during Q2 2027 as compared to corresponding quarter last year.
Let's not look to guide this business every quarter, for the next two quarters.
Every INR10 increase in cane price will result into INR100 crores of incremental raw material cost.
Logically, physically understood with the supplier, much lower.
